title: Committee of Supply − Head K (Ministry of Education)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply − Head K (Ministry of Education)

sections.label: Future schools and reskilling
sections.summary: The speaker moves a $100 reduction and urges MOE to assemble a team to study how future schools should look, citing the World Economic Forum's call to rethink education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head K of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We heard the mantra: "disruptions are occurring at breakneck pace and if we do not retool, reskill ourselves, the likes of Ubers, Grabs, AirBnB, TripAdvsors, Alibabas will soon be eating our lunch!" Sir, I urge the Ministry of Education (MOE) to assemble a team of external and internal parties to take a deeper look at how schools for the future ought to look like, how different they are from the schools of today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The World Economic Forum (WEF), in a paper on the future of jobs, had called for a rethinking of education systems.

sections.label: Reskilling ageing workforces
sections.summary: The report says ageing countries need wholesale reskilling of existing workforces throughout their lifecycle, and schools for the future must be Schools FOR Life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The report says, "Ageing countries would not just need lifelong learning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: They will need wholesale reskilling of existing workforces throughout their lifecycle." Schools for the future must surely be Schools FOR Life.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and lifelong learners
sections.summary: The definition of education has expanded beyond traditional age limits through SkillsFuture, though creating a nation of lifelong learners remains a long way off.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Our definition of education, for instance, has expanded to more than the traditional limits of age through the SkillsFuture initiative.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We are still a long way, of course, to creating a nation of learners who do not just carry an L-plate but we need to cherry Triple L-plates, which stands for Life Long Learners, Triple L.

sections.label: Reviewing schools for the future
sections.summary: The speaker asks what roles educators, employers and families play, says sacred cows like high-stakes exams cannot be ignored, and urges MOE to assemble a review team.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: What are the roles, competencies and contributions of the partners of our schools for the future − the educators, employers and the families?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We cannot afford to ignore sacred cows we reared − the high-stakes exams, the direct admission system, the over-reliance on tuition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We need to dare, we need to imagine, we need to innovate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We need an Industry Transformation Map (ITM) that includes the MOE professionals and partners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We need to build schools poised for the future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I, therefore, urge MOE again to assemble a team to review, reflect and report on how ready our education institutions are, indeed, for the future.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the development of values and good character has always been a cornerstone of our education system.

sections.label: How children learn values
sections.summary: Children learn values and develop character through three ways: understanding, observing and doing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Children learn values and develop character through three ways: understanding, observing and doing.

sections.label: Role modelling internalises values
sections.summary: Behavioural psychologists have found that role modelling is the most effective way of helping children internalise values and develop character.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Behavioural psychologists have found that role modelling is the most effective way of helping children internalise values and develop character.

sections.label: Values in Action and NurtureSG
sections.summary: Values in Action in schools is described as intent, and NurtureSG means children must learn personal health responsibility and peer support.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: That, I believe, is the intent of Values in Action in our schools.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Now, with the announcement of NurtureSG, our children also need to learn about taking personal responsibility for their health and extending peer support to their friends to do so.

sections.label: Dimmed fire in schools
sections.summary: The fire in the sporting belly of our schools has dimmed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The fire in the sporting belly of our schools has dimmed.

sections.label: Entrepreneurship programmes for students
sections.summary: The Government should progressively develop entrepreneurship programmes from primary to tertiary levels for every student to inspire more entrepreneurs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government should develop such entrepreneurship programmes progressively for different levels from primary school upwards to tertiary levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I believe that making such programmes available to every student will bring benefit not just by way of general education and exposure, but from this much larger pool of students exposed to such education, we should be able to inspire many more young Singaporeans to be entrepreneurs and/or to develop a nose for businesses.

sections.label: Academic streaming pigeonholes students
sections.summary: Academic streaming tends to pigeonhole students and place expectations about their intelligence or abilities according to their stream.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: Academic streaming tends to pigeonhole students and inadvertently place expectations about their intelligence or abilities according to the stream they are in.

sections.label: Abolish academic streaming
sections.summary: Given different pathways, peaks of excellence, subject-based banding and discretionary admission, it is time to abolish academic streaming and continue with subject-based banding.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: With our emphasis on different educational pathways and different peaks of excellence in education, as well as subject-based banding and discretionary admission to schools, I believe it is time we take this leap of faith to abolish academic streaming in our schools and instead continue with just subject-based banding.

sections.label: Primary school mathematics word problems
sections.summary: Parents shared that primary school mathematics word problems can be very complicated, testing English comprehension as well as numeracy and mathematics.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Parents have shared with me about word problems in primary school mathematics, which can be very complicated.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I worry that such word problems are not just a test of numeracy and mathematics, they test English comprehension as well.

sections.label: Private tuition industry size
sections.summary: The private tuition industry is said to be at least $1.1 billion large and is called the shadow education industry by some.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: The private tuition industry, said to be at least $1.1 billion large, is described as the shadow education industry by some.

sections.label: Self-help groups and MOE review
sections.summary: Self-help groups CDAC, MENDAKI and SINDA have supported students needing extra help, and it is time MOE reviewed its position of ignoring the tuition industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: In fact, the self-help groups, such as the Chinese Development Assistance Council (CDAC), the Council on Education for Muslim Children (MENDAKI) and the Singapore Indian Development Association (SINDA) have done good work supporting students who need the extra help.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: It is time that MOE review its position of ignoring the tuition industry, especially publicly.

sections.label: Accelerate e-campus setup
sections.summary: One proposal is to accelerate setting up an e-campus so students and MOE staff and stakeholders can access good quality learning materials.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: One, accelerate the setting up of an e-campus so that students and other MOE staff and stakeholders can help themselves to good quality learning materials with content good enough that the typical students would not require to spend to go for tuition.

sections.label: Engage private tuition industry
sections.summary: A fourth proposal is to study ways to engage the private tuition industry and set ground rules for quality and affordability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Four, study ways by which the private tuition industry can be engaged and set up ground rules to ensure quality and affordability.

sections.label: Baseline funding for schools
sections.summary: Per capita funding for students may seem fair at the micro level, but at the macro level there has to be baseline funding for schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
sentences.text: The per capita funding for students may seem fair at the micro level but, at the macro level, there has to be a baseline funding for schools.

sections.label: MOE PSLE system changes
sections.summary: In July 2016, MOE announced changes to the PSLE system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In July 2016, MOE announced changes to the PSLE system.

sections.label: PSLE scoring bands and school cut-offs
sections.summary: MOE moves to wider scoring bands, yet schools are told there is no scope for appeal if a student misses the cut-off point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Some people believe that a student who scores 231 points is better than another student who scores 230, but it is not educationally meaningful to differentiate so finely between the two at this age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Hence, we are moving to wider scoring bands, where students in the same band are similar academically." MOE wants parents to believe that it is not necessary to chase after the last mark in the PSLE exam and that "Primary school education is a time when students develop foundational language and numeracy skills." But yet, after PSLE results are released, every school is told that if the student does not meet the cut-off point for the school, there is no scope for appeal.

sections.label: Appeals for near cut-off students
sections.summary: MOE should let students one or two points from a school's cut-off point demonstrate their ability to principals through interview or assessment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: MOE should allow these students who are not too far off from the cut-off point of the school, maybe just one or two points away, to demonstrate their ability to the principals through an interview or some form of assessment.

sections.label: DSA applications in 2016
sections.summary: In 2016, 16,000 students tried to apply to a choice of secondary schools through the DSA scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Chairman, in 2016, 16,000 students tried to apply to a choice of secondary schools through the DSA scheme.

sections.label: GEP students admitted to IP schools
sections.summary: GEP primary students are automatically admitted to IP schools of their choice even if they scored badly in the PSLE, without entrance tests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: At the other extreme, it is an open secret that Gifted Education Programme (GEP) students in primary schools are automatically admitted to IP schools of their choice, even if they scored badly in the PSLE, and they do not need to sit for entrance tests.

sections.label: DSA in admission ecosystem
sections.summary: Since 2004 the DSA system has become part of the admission ecosystem, and 2016 saw a record number of DSA applications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Since 2004, the DSA system has become part of that admission ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: It is, therefore, no surprise that 2016 saw a record number of applications by PSLE students for DSA into a school of their choice.

sections.label: DSA Academic and diversity
sections.summary: DSA Academic does nothing to enhance diversity because the PSLE is itself based entirely on academic merit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: DSA Academic, however, does absolutely nothing to enhance that diversity because the PSLE is itself based entirely on academic merit.

sections.label: DSA CCA commitment requirement
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to review requiring DSA Sport or Performing Arts students to stay in that field for four to six years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Second, can the Minister also review the requirement that a student who gains admission into a school in DSA Sport or Performing Arts is required to stick to that chosen field for the next four to six years and not replace it with any other co-curricular activities (CCAs)?

sections.label: Affiliated and non-affiliated entry scores
sections.summary: Entry scores for affiliated and non-affiliated pupils can differ by up to 40 points, with CHIJ Toa Payoh cited as an example.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The entry scores for affiliated and non-affiliated pupils at some schools can vary by as much as 40 points.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For example, in last year's exercise for entry into the Convent for the Holy Infant Jesus (CHIJ) Secondary (Toa Payoh), affiliated pupils need only a T-score of 200 to get into the Express stream while non-affiliated pupils must score at least 247 and above to get a place in Express stream.

sections.label: Fairness in school affiliation
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked what assurance it can give parents of non-affiliated children about equal opportunities to enrol in popular schools.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: While we recognise the purpose of affiliation and its role in developing values and culture that are aligned to the religious or clan association that the affiliated schools come under, we must also strive to ensure fairness and accessibility to popular schools for all our students.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: What assurance can the Ministry provide to parents whose children are not in affiliated schools that their children will not in any way be deprived of equal opportunities to enrol in a popular school of their choice?

sections.label: Allied Educators in schools
sections.summary: All primary schools and most secondary schools have at least one Allied Educator.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Today, all primary schools and most secondary schools are resourced with at least one Allied Educator.

sections.label: Tertiary employer handshake framework
sections.summary: Handshakes between tertiary students and employers are weak, so a more robust framework of services, standards and training is needed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Handshakes between tertiary level students and the employers are either non-existent or quite weak, making internships and eventual employment dicey and at risk of failing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: There is a strong need to develop a more robust framework of a minimum core set of services, standards and training.

sections.label: Establishing a SPED Academy
sections.summary: The speaker believes the best strategy is a SPED Academy cutting across all Ministries, led by passionate members with relevant networks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: On the SPED Academy, I believe that the best strategy is to establish a SPED Academy that will cut across all Ministries and led by members with strong passion and relevant networks.

sections.label: Dyslexia diagnosis and schemes
sections.summary: Schemes may be extended to VWO day activity centres and sheltered workshops, with about 1,600 children per cohort possibly having severe dyslexia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: If successful, such schemes can be extended to day activity centres and sheltered workshops for persons with disabilities operated by VWOs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This would mean that there are about 1,600 children per cohort in Singapore who may have severe dyslexia.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It was reported last year that the Dyslexia Association of Singapore (DAS) has been assessing around 900 students each year, of which two-thirds are diagnosed with dyslexia.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This means that there could be hundreds of children per cohort who have the condition but are not diagnosed.

sections.label: Programme take-up rate
sections.summary: Only 1,000 of an expected 4,000 people have been placed under the programme, a small fraction of the $30 million set aside.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: The take-up rate to date is but a small fraction of the $30 million set aside for the programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Only 1,000 out of an expected number of 4,000 people have been placed under the programme by last month.

sections.label: MOE and partner kindergartens
sections.summary: There are currently 15 MOE-run kindergartens and 169 run by partner operators.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: Currently, there are 15 MOE-run kindergartens and there are 169 run by partner operators.

sections.label: MOE overseas school
sections.summary: The only overseas school run by MOE is in Hong Kong.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: At the moment, the only overseas school run by MOE is in Hong Kong.

sections.label: Children's school and sleep
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked how it will ensure children are sent to school, and they get five to six hours of the recommended eight hours of sleep.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: How will the Ministry ensure that children are sent to school?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: They are getting around five to six hours of the recommended eight hours of sleep.

sections.label: School start times and after-school care
sections.summary: Most schools start at 7.30 am, and only slightly more than half of 15,000 former full-day preschool students got after-school care places.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: Currently, most of our schools start at 7.30 am, which means that students would wake up before sunrise, resulting in a disruption to their circadian rhythms.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: If we can start schools an hour later at 8.30 am, students will no longer need to wake up before sunrise and this could help improve their sleep cycles, thus leading to better health and learning outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: About 15,000 Singaporean children, or 45% of the cohort, were enrolled in a full-day preschool programme at Kindergarten (K)2 level in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: From the answer to a Parliamentary Question I filed last year to MOE, around 7,800 Primary 1 students are enrolled in Student Care Centres (SCCs) registered with the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF).

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: Among these students, 4,800 are enrolled in school-based SCCs whilst the rest are enrolled in community-based SCCs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: This means that only slightly more than half of the 15,000 students who were previously in full day preschool at K2 managed to get a place in an after-school care centre.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: Although MOE has increased the number of school-based SCCs from less than 50 five years ago to 147 today, the overall enrolment has risen from 3,000 to more than 18,000.

sections.label: Student care centres in primary schools
sections.summary: The passage asks when all 190 primary schools will have student care centres.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: When can we see all our 190 primary schools have their student care centres?

sections.label: Evolving parent involvement in schools
sections.summary: The passage states that parent involvement in schools is evolving as parents are better educated and more well-informed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The nature of parent involvement in schools is evolving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Parents today are better educated and more well-informed.

sections.label: Parent Support Groups in schools
sections.summary: The passage asks how MOE can help schools build strong PSG networks and how PSGs can be more effective in school involvement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Many schools tap on the Parent Support Groups (PSGs) to support school programmes and activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: How can MOE help schools build strong networks with PSGs which can then be a bridge between the school and other parents?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: How can PSGs be more effective in the school involvement?

sections.label: Daily cleaning in schools
sections.summary: The passage states that daily cleaning was introduced in schools last year to instil personal and social responsibility in children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Last year, we introduced daily cleaning in schools to instil in our children a stronger sense of personal and social responsibility.

sections.label: Committee for the Future Economy roadmap
sections.summary: The passage states the Committee for the Future Economy recently outlined a roadmap on evolving to meet future economic challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The Committee for the Future Economy (CFE) recently outlined a roadmap on how we need to evolve to meet the economic challenges of the future.

sections.label: Shift to holistic education
sections.summary: The passage states that last year Minister Ong and the speaker talked about shifting away from over-emphasis on academic grades to holistic education.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Last year, Minister Ong and I talked about making a paradigm shift away from an over-emphasis on academic grades, to focus on holistic education.

sections.label: Programme for Active Learning
sections.summary: The Programme for Active Learning in every primary school combines classroom learning with outdoor activities, and applied learning is encouraged for upper primary and secondary students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The Programme for Active Learning in every primary school provides varied and fun learning experiences, combining classroom learning with outdoor activities to stimulate interest and curiosity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Two, we are encouraging more applied learning among our upper primary and secondary school students so that they do not just learn theories but get to apply learning to real-world contexts.

sections.label: Excessive tuition erodes joy
sections.summary: Excessive tuition, especially when the child is already doing well, can erode the joy of learning.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Excessive tuition, especially when the child is already doing well, can erode the joy of learning.

sections.label: Online portal and levelling-up programmes
sections.summary: Schools are developing an online portal for self-paced learning and provide levelling-up programmes, remedial and consultation sessions for students needing extra help.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: In schools, we are calibrating this balance carefully.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We are developing an online portal for all students to support their self-paced learning and revision.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: For those students who require extra help, we provide levelling-up programmes in smaller groups, and remedial and consultation sessions outside of lesson time.

sections.label: PSLE T-score replaced
sections.summary: From 2021, the PSLE T-score will be replaced with wider Achievement Levels, and pupils will be assessed independently of their peers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: From 2021 onwards, the PSLE T-score will be replaced with wider Achievement Levels, and pupils will be assessed independently of how their peers fare.

sections.label: Simplifying mathematics problem language
sections.summary: Schools and teachers are guided and trained to pitch school-based assessments closer to national examination standards, and language in mathematics problems has been simplified.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We guide schools and provide training and resources to teachers to help them pitch school-based assessments closer to the standards of the national examinations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: I would also like to assure Dr Tan Wu Meng that we have taken active steps to simplify the language used to set mathematics problems in national examinations.

sections.label: Outdoor education builds character
sections.summary: Outdoor education and adventure build character qualities such as resilience, tenacity, leadership, teamwork, grit and adaptability, and 28 schools' Secondary 3 students will join the MOE-OBS programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Apart from being fun, outdoor education and adventure build character and qualities, such as resilience, tenacity, leadership, teamwork, grit and adaptability, all of which help to foster entrepreneurial dare.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: This year, I am happy to see that Secondary 3 students from 28 schools will take part in the new five-day MOE-Outward Bound School (OBS) programme.

sections.label: Outdoor adventure programme for Secondary 3
sections.summary: The programme is on track to become a common experience for all Secondary 3 students from 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Having nurtured a strong team of passionate and qualified outdoor adventure educators, we are on track to make this programme a common experience for all Secondary 3 students from 2020.

sections.label: Increased PE lessons
sections.summary: Physical education lessons have been increased to at least two hours per week across all levels.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Across all levels, we have increased physical education (PE) lessons to at least two hours per week.

sections.label: Sports CCAs and National School Games
sections.summary: More than 60 sports CCAs are offered, and over 55,000 student athletes participate yearly in the National School Games.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Today, we have more than 60 sports CCAs being offered across our schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Each year, more than 55,000 student athletes participate in the numerous sporting events in the National School Games.

sections.label: Subject-Based Banding for Secondary 1
sections.summary: By 2018, Subject-Based Banding will be implemented for Secondary 1 students in all secondary schools offering Normal courses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: By 2018, we will implement Subject-Based Banding for Secondary 1 students in all secondary schools that offer the Normal (Academic) and Normal (Technical) courses.

sections.label: Three secondary school courses
sections.summary: The Express, Normal (Academic) and Normal (Technical) courses cater to different learning needs and have kept attrition rates below 1%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The three courses − Express, Normal (Academic) and Normal (Technical) − have catered to the different learning needs and pace of our students and have succeeded in keeping students engaged in schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: This allows them to progress as far as possible in their studies and, as a result, our attrition rates today are very, very low, at less than 1%, compared to 30%-40% at the start of our education journey.

sections.label: Expanding Subject-Based Banding
sections.summary: By 2018, Subject-Based Banding will be expanded to all schools to benefit more students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Hearing the girls' positive experiences, I am glad that, by 2018, we will be able to expand Subject-Based Banding to all schools, to benefit more students.

sections.label: Appeals and school transfers
sections.summary: Flexibility is exercised for students with medical or special needs or exceptional circumstances, and over 400 students appealed successfully and obtained a school transfer.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: For those who do not meet the cut-off point, flexibility will be exercised if they have medical or special needs, or if there are exceptional circumstances.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Over 400 of our students appealed successfully and obtained a school transfer, according to their school preferences.

sections.label: DSA secondary school admissions
sections.summary: Many students made multiple applications, and a total of 2,800 students were admitted to secondary school via DSA, half to the Integrated Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: That means many students actually made multiple applications.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: So, eventually, a total of 2,800 students were admitted to secondary school via DSA, half of which were to the Integrated Programme (IP).

sections.label: Expanding DSA places from 2018
sections.summary: From 2018, all secondary schools can admit up to 20% of their Secondary 1, non-IP intake via DSA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Starting from 2018, we will expand the number of DSA places so that all secondary schools can admit up to 20% of their Secondary 1, non-IP intake via DSA.

sections.label: DSA selection and academic tests
sections.summary: Schools will focus on specific talents and discontinue general academic ability tests in DSA selection by 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Schools will focus on identifying students with specific talents and move away from recognising strong general academic abilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: As part of this refinement, schools will discontinue the use of general academic ability tests in DSA selection by 2018.

sections.label: Centralised DSA online application portal
sections.summary: From the 2019 DSA Exercise, students can submit applications through a centralised online portal using a common application form.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: From the 2019 DSA Exercise onwards, students will be able to submit their applications through a centralised online application portal, using a common application form.

sections.label: Special needs and financial assistance
sections.summary: Children with moderate to severe Special Educational Needs will be included in the Compulsory Education Act, and FAS was enhanced with transport and meal subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Last year, we announced that we will include children with moderate to severe Special Educational Needs in the Compulsory Education (CE) Act.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: In 2015, we enhanced the MOE Financial Assistance Scheme (FAS) to include a transport subsidy, in the form of a $120 public transport credit or a 50% subsidy for their school bus fee.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: In 2016, we also doubled the overall meal subsidy provision, from $270 to $520 per year for every primary school student on FAS, to support more meals and at a higher value.

sections.label: Specialised Schools funding Crest Spectra
sections.summary: Crest and Spectra, Specialised Schools for Normal (Technical) students, received about $27,000 per capita funding in FY 2016, higher than other schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Take, for instance, the four Specialised Schools, in particular, Crest and Spectra, which we have set up for students in the Normal (Technical) course.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: They received per capita funding of about $27,000 in financial year (FY) 2016, significantly higher than other schools.

sections.label: Affiliated secondary school places reserved
sections.summary: From the 2019 Secondary 1 Posting Exercise, 20% of places per course in every affiliated secondary school are reserved for students without affiliation priority.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Starting from the 2019 Secondary 1 Posting Exercise, 20% of places for each course in every affiliated secondary school will be reserved for students who do not benefit from affiliation priority.

sections.label: Higher subject levels and DSA expansion
sections.summary: From 2018, lower secondary students can take stronger subjects at a higher level if they meet criteria, and DSA opportunities will be expanded.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: From 2018, lower secondary students will have the flexibility to take their stronger subjects at a higher level, as long as they meet the criteria.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: In 2018, we will also expand opportunities for DSA, students can better access to a secondary school with suitable programmes to nurture their talents and achievements.

sections.label: Singapore International School Hong Kong only overseas MOE school
sections.summary: SISHK is the only overseas school run by MOE for Singaporean students abroad, and there are no plans to set up a similar school elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The Singapore International School Hong Kong (SISHK) is the only overseas school run by MOE to cater to Singaporean students who are based abroad.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We currently do not have plans to set up a similar school elsewhere.

sections.label: Horseshoe crab blue blood extract value
sections.summary: Students learnt that horseshoe crabs' blue blood has medicinal value and are learning to harvest the extract, valued at over US$15,000 per litre.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Along the way, they also learnt that the blue blood of horseshoe crabs has special medicinal value.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: They are now learning how to harvest the blue blood extract which is valued at over US$15,000 per litre.

sections.label: MOE support for SEN students
sections.summary: MOE is committed to helping students needing more attention and support, and to supporting the education of all students with special educational needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: MOE is also committed to helping those in our schools who may need more attention and support to access these opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: I assure Ms Denise Phua that MOE is committed to supporting the education of all our students with special educational needs (SEN).

sections.label: MOE special education school support
sections.summary: MOE shares evidence-based practices among school personnel and works with partners to improve MOE-funded special education schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Besides training, MOE also facilitates the sharing of evidence-based practice and strategies that work well amongst school personnel.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We have always been working closely with our partners to improve the quality, accessibility and affordability of MOE-funded special education (SPED) schools and to enable our students to realise their potential for independent living.

sections.label: PSEA use broadened
sections.summary: MOE has broadened the Post-Secondary Education Account to include approved training courses under SG Enable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: MOE has also broadened the use of the Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) to include approved training courses under SG Enable.

sections.label: MOE employs persons with disabilities
sections.summary: MOE currently employs 80 persons with disabilities, in response to Mr Dennis Tan's question.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: In response to Mr Dennis Tan's question, MOE currently employs 80 persons with disabilities.

sections.label: FLAiR beneficiaries since 2007
sections.summary: Since 2007, FLAiR has benefited more than 21,000 children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Since 2007, FLAiR has benefited more than 21,000 children.

sections.label: Holistic approach to non-attendance
sections.summary: MOE works with parents, schools, Family Service Centres and agencies to support attendance, with legal enforcement as a last resort.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Imposing penalties, as provided for under the Act, does not necessarily solve the root problems of non-attendance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: MOE takes a holistic approach by working together with parents, schools, the Family Service Centres (FSCs) and relevant agencies to counsel and support the family and help all students attend school.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Legal enforcement should be the last resort, considered only if all possible interventions and counselling efforts have been exhausted.

sections.label: School-based SCC expansion
sections.summary: School-based SCCs increased to 147, supporting over 18,000 students, with SCCs in all primary schools targeted by end-2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Over the last five years, we have increased the number of school-based SCCs to 147, supporting more than 18,000 students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The provision has largely kept pace with demand and we remain on track to open SCCs in all primary schools by the end of 2020 and will continue to work with the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) to monitor the demand for SCC places in our schools and in the community.

sections.label: SkillsFuture reskilling and employability
sections.summary: It says reskilling must keep pace with technology and that SkillsFuture should focus less on courses and credit and more on linking training to employability and re-employment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: It will enable them to be reskilled multiple times in their working life to keep pace with technological advancement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, more must be done to shift the focus of SkillsFuture away from the long list of SkillsFuture courses available and how one can spend the $500 SkillsFuture Credit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I have spoken often about the use of SkillsFuture to help retrenched professionals find their feet, rebuild their confidence, guide them to acquire new skills and, most importantly, to get employers to provide job opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: There should be a strong connection between training and employability, a direct line of sight between the efforts that one puts into retraining and the hope of re-employment.

sections.label: National training programme registry
sections.summary: It asks whether the Government will set up a national registry to grade, rank and publish training programme effectiveness so workers can choose, with good outcomes possibly getting more subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Will the Government consider setting up a national registry to grade, rank and publish the effectiveness of different training programmes so that workers can make an informed choice?

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Programmes with positive employment outcomes may be listed as such and may even offer more generous subsidies.

sections.label: Industry competency standards alignment
sections.summary: It states the SkillsFuture movement should accelerate building competency standards within each industry and key families so curriculum and training align with current and future job requirements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture movement should accelerate the building of competency standards within each industry and key families to ensure that curriculum development and training efforts are closely aligned with current and future job requirements.

sections.label: Women in IT enrolment
sections.summary: It states that in 2015, 43 women per 100 men enrolled in IT first and higher degrees, and 58 females per 100 male students in diploma courses.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2015, only 43 women out of every 100 men enrolled in the information technology (IT) field for their first and higher degrees, and only 58 females for every 100 male students enrolled for the diploma courses.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit utilisation numbers
sections.summary: It states that a Parliamentary Question on SkillsFuture Credit utilisation reported over 80,000 Singaporeans had used them up to August 2016, later revised to 126,000 for the entire year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end and in October last year, I asked a Parliamentary Question about the utilisation of SkillsFuture Credits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was reported that up to August 2016, over 80,000 Singaporeans had used them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This number was later revised on the back of a similar Parliamentary Question this year which raised the number to 126,000 over the course of the entire year.

sections.label: Breakdown of funded training places
sections.summary: It states the Government funded 920,000 training places in 2015 and asks the Minister for a breakdown by industry and plans moving forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, it was recently reported that the Government funded 920,000 training places in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide a breakdown of these numbers and which industries received the most and, conversely, the least attention as well, and what are its plans moving forward?

sections.label: Training attendance record high
sections.summary: 42% of the labour force aged 15 to 64 attended training in the year ending June 2016, a record high versus 35% the previous year.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Forty-two percent of our labour force aged 15 to 64 attended training over the year ending June 2016, a record high, compared to 35% the previous year.

sections.label: SkillsFuture course quality and marriage target
sections.summary: It asks how MOE and SSG ensure quality, market-relevant SkillsFuture courses, and notes difficulty reaching the 1.4 to 1.5 marriage target set in 2013.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: How do MOE and SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) ensure the provision of high-quality SkillsFuture courses that are relevant to market needs and help individuals make informed decisions on training and careers?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We are struggling to reach the 1.4 to 1.5 mark that Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean set as the target back in 2013 when launching the Marriage and Parenthood package.

sections.label: SkillsFuture award and education loan
sections.summary: It proposes a one-year award coinciding with no-pay leave in the baby's first year and a SkillsFuture Education Loan for courses with hefty fees.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The award would be valid for one year, which should coincide with the no-pay leave period during the baby's first year, an idea mooted by the Government last year and is currently being explored.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While many local courses are subsidised for Singaporeans and the Government has provided some assistance by way of the SkillsFuture Credit, there are courses that still require hefty fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I would, therefore, like to propose the Government setting up a SkillsFuture Education Loan to facilitate further and continuing education that will help workers to advance their careers or switch career paths.

sections.label: CPF Education Scheme scope
sections.summary: The CPF Education Scheme is for full-time subsidised courses at Approved Educational Institutions and applies only to first degrees and diplomas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The CPF Education Scheme is meant for full-time subsidised courses offered at Approved Educational Institutions and only applies for first degrees and diplomas.

sections.label: Swiss work-study training benefits
sections.summary: It says Swiss early practical training is a key competitive advantage, and blending work and study gives better employment, job matching and lifelong learning preparation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: Having seen how Swiss students are trained from an early age to master practical skills in a real-life work environment, I am convinced that this is the key competitive advantage that has helped Switzerland to become one of the most competitive economies in the world.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: There are many advantages in blending work and study into degree programmes, such as better employment prospects, better job matching and better preparation to embrace lifelong learning.

sections.label: Hands-on polytechnic diploma courses
sections.summary: It suggests MOE consider technical, hands-on diploma courses for hands-on learners, focusing on deepening skills rather than pen-and-pencil examinations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, diploma courses in the local polytechnics may not suit them, as they are more adept at hands-on learning and are less academically inclined.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to suggest that MOE consider devising diploma courses that are technical and hands-on in nature, which focus on deepening skills rather than pen-and-pencil examinations.

sections.label: Education roles government industry
sections.summary: The government handles basic and tertiary education, while industry associations handle vocational education and worker training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The government is responsible for basic education and tertiary education, while the industry associations cater to vocational education and worker training.

sections.label: ITE polytechnic trade association collaboration
sections.summary: The speaker suggests ITEs and polytechnics work together with trade associations, citing the German experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Taking a leaf from the German experience, I suggest that ITEs and polytechnics work together on a win-win basis to strengthen collaboration with trade associations.

sections.label: NUS NTU ranking improvements
sections.summary: NUS rose from 40th in 2011 to 24th in 2016, and NTU from 174th to 54th.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: According to the Times Higher Education World University Rankings, NUS was ranked 40th in 2011 and now ranked 24th in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: NTU was ranked 174th in 2011 and is now ranked 54th, that is, NTU jumped 120 places in five years.

sections.label: University research priorities and grant calls
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Minister refocuses local university research on Singapore challenges rather than rankings, noting about 70 grant proposals await announcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: I hope the Minister can consider refocusing the priorities of the local universities so that they can conduct research which would help us to better understand and perhaps even solve challenges faced by Singapore and Singaporeans, rather than in pure pursuit of global university rankings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I understand the first round of grant calls has closed to about 70 proposals and an announcement is due soon on the award recipients.

sections.label: Hybrid academic aptitude admissions system
sections.summary: The speaker suggests MOE adopt a hybrid system weighting 60% academic and 40% aptitude, as pure aptitude-based admission may be subjective.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: However, a pure aptitude-based system may be too subjective as it is dependent on the assessors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I suggest MOE adopt a hybrid system, perhaps with 60% weight towards academic and 40% weight to aptitude.

sections.label: Aptitude-based admissions quota increase
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the quota allocated for Aptitude-based Admissions can be increased.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Can we do more and increase the quota allocated for Aptitude-based Admissions?

sections.label: University tuition fee increases
sections.summary: In 2007 NUS, NTU and SMU charged Singaporeans about $7,000 to $8,000 yearly for general arts and science degrees, with fees rising about 38% over 10 years, outpacing CPI growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: In 2007, the three major Singapore universities − NUS, NTU and the Singapore Management University (SMU) − charged Singaporeans roughly $7,000 to $8,000 in annual tuition for a general arts and science degree.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Fees in the last 10 years have gone up about 38% on average and the increase varies across institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: What is consistent, however, is that the increase in the tuition fee has significantly outpaced consumer price index (CPI) growth over the same period.

sections.label: MOE financial support criteria
sections.summary: The speaker says private donor funding may not be sustainable and asks the Minister to relax qualifying criteria for MOE's financial support for tertiary students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: However, raising funds through private donors may not be sustainable and is especially difficult when the economy is slowing down.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Thus, I hope that the Minister can relax the qualifying criteria for MOE's financial support for tertiary students so that more can benefit.

sections.label: Transforming higher education landscape
sections.summary: The speaker says the higher education landscape must be transformed, with education also a journey to fulfil hopes and aspirations and learning being lifelong.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We need to transform our higher education landscape in response.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We need to make five important shifts as part of this transformation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: One, besides being a pathway into good jobs and lifelong employability, education also needs to be a journey to fulfil hopes and aspirations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Two, education and learning need to be lifelong.

sections.label: Education must impart skills
sections.summary: The speaker states that education must impart skills, not just information and knowledge.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Third, education must impart skills, not just information and knowledge, for a simple reason.

sections.label: Changes over next five years
sections.summary: The speaker says the changes will take place over the next five years and will set the stage for continued progress for the next 20.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The changes will take place over the next five years but will set the stage for our continued progress for the next 20.

sections.label: Bill to restructure UniSIM
sections.summary: The speaker will table a Bill this year to restructure the Singapore Institute of Management (UniSIM) into the sixth AU, focusing on applied degree programmes in the social sciences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Later this year, I will be tabling a Bill in this House to restructure the Singapore Institute of Management (UniSIM) into our sixth AU, which will focus on applied degree programmes in the social sciences, such as social work, HR, psychology, early childhood education and so on.

sections.label: Supply-side funding and training participation
sections.summary: The approach leans on supply-side funding, with $400 million yearly versus $37 million for SkillsFuture Credit, and training participation rose from 32% to 42%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: On balance, our approach is to continue to lean more on supply-side funding, which is more prudent and a stronger lever in public policymaking.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, today, we spend about $400 million a year on supply-side funding, versus $37 million last year on SkillsFuture Credit funding.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Through our efforts to promote Lifelong Learning and SkillsFuture over the years, our training participation rate has jumped from 32% to 42% over 10 years, and half of the increase was realised in the last three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Training headcounts annually have increased by 70% to 380,000 today, over the last five years.

sections.label: Preference for supply-side measures
sections.summary: The preference is to rely mainly on supply-side measures, with some 9,000 courses already heavily subsidised.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But we would rather do so mainly from supply-side measures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: There are some 9,000 courses out there which are already heavily subsidised.

sections.label: Enhanced Government bursaries from 2017
sections.summary: MOE reviewed Government bursaries and will enhance them from academic year 2017 by introducing four bursary tiers across all PSEIs and using gross monthly household income.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: MOE has reviewed the Government bursaries and will enhance it in the following ways from academic year 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: First, we will introduce four bursary tiers across all PSEIs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Second, besides per capita income, we will also look at gross monthly household income.

sections.label: Bursary increase amounts by income
sections.summary: The increase will range between $50 and $400 across various levels, with larger increases for lower-income students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The increase will range between $50 and $400 across various levels, with larger increases going to the lower-income students.

sections.label: Projected bursary student numbers
sections.summary: With the revisions, the projected number of students tapping the bursaries will increase by 12,000 per year to 71,000 per year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: With the revisions, the projected number of students expected to tap on the bursaries will increase by 12,000 per year to 71,000 per year.

sections.label: Polytechnics EAE quota increase
sections.summary: Given first-year success, MOE will increase the polytechnics EAE quota from 12.5% to 15% for the 2018 Admission Year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Given the success in the first year of implementation, MOE will increase the polytechnics EAE quota from 12.5% to 15% for the 2018 Admission Year.

sections.label: ITE EAE aptitude admissions
sections.summary: MOE will introduce an ITE EAE so ITEs can systematically admit up to 15% of intake via aptitude-based admissions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: MOE will, therefore, introduce an ITE EAE, where the ITEs can systematically admit up to 15% of its intake via aptitude-based admissions.

sections.label: ITE Technical Diploma pathway
sections.summary: A new ITE-conferred Technical Diploma pathway will be developed, apprenticeship-based and differing from polytechnic Diplomas in mode of learning.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: These are distinctly different paths to the top, via development of cognitive abilities through formal education, or via "learning by doing" in a structured and facilitated way.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Hence, we will develop a new pathway for ITE students leading to a Technical Diploma that will be conferred by ITE.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Compared to a polytechnic Diploma, the big difference is in the mode of learning, it will be apprenticeship-based.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Work-study Degree Programmes
sections.summary: At SIT's first graduation ceremony, it was announced that SIT and UniSIM will introduce seven new SkillsFuture Work-study Degree Programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: When I attended SIT's very first graduation ceremony recently, I announced that SIT and UniSIM will introduce seven new SkillsFuture Work-study Degree Programmes.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Engage community outreach
sections.summary: SkillsFuture Engage will have SSG partner PA, CDCs, Workforce Singapore and e2i to conduct community workshops, reaching tens of thousands yearly from mid-year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It will help us reach out to more workers, which Miss Cheng Li Hui spoke about.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: I announced the effort called SkillsFuture Engage last year, where we will proactively step up efforts to connect with Singaporeans and help them benefit from SkillsFuture.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: SSG will partner the People's Association (PA), CDCs, Workforce Singapore and e2i, to conduct workshops at the community level to explain SkillsFuture to Singaporeans, guide them in finding the right training programmes to attend, identify the right skills for them to learn and advise them how to best use their SkillsFuture Credit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We expect to reach out to tens of thousands of Singaporeans each year through this initiative and roll out the programme in the middle of this year.

sections.label: Future@Work national training programme
sections.summary: SSG is developing Future@Work, a new national training programme positioned as an entry programme for all Singaporean workers, launching by year-end.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: SSG is developing it and will roll this out as a new national training programme and they called it Future@Work.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It will be implemented across the island and positioned as an entry programme for all Singaporean workers to understand the future work environment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We plan to launch the programme by the end of this year.

sections.label: SSRC supports Humanities research
sections.summary: Despite its name, the SSRC is meant to support the Humanities too and will fund good research projects in these disciplines.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding its name, the SSRC is meant to support the Humanities, too, and will fund good research projects in these disciplines.
